title: How Much of a Surplus on the Medical Plan Bill is Carried to the Rider
content:
Where money left over stands on a member's Medicare Advantage Health Plans bill — that is, where the payments booked on that enrollment's premium account come to more than the medical plan premium charged on it — some of it may be carried toward the rider premium owed on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders.

## The rule

1. Where the money left over on the medical plan bill comes to more than the rider premium charged that is counted, the amount carried is the rider premium charged that is counted.
2. Where the medical plan bill carries money received against it and the money left over does not come to more than that, the amount carried is the whole of the money left over on the medical plan bill.
3. Otherwise the amount carried is nothing, no money having been received on the medical plan bill.

## Restated as a ceiling and a floor

The amount carried never exceeds the rider premium charged that is counted, and never exceeds the money left over on the medical plan bill; where the bill carries no money received against it at all, nothing is carried whatever else stands.

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

Take rider premium charged that is counted of 57.20 USD.

| Money left over on the medical plan bill | Money received on that bill | Amount carried |
|---|---|---|
| 90.00 USD | yes | 57.20 USD, the rider premium charged that is counted |
| 30.00 USD | yes | 30.00 USD, the whole of the money left over |
| 57.20 USD | yes | 57.20 USD, the whole of the money left over |
| 0.00 USD | yes | Nothing |
| 40.00 USD | no | Nothing, no money having been received on the medical plan bill |

The third row sits on the boundary: the money left over does not come to more than the rider premium charged that is counted, so the whole of it is carried, which comes to the same figure either way.
